system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Scope:** I reviewed the Seller's Update summary and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) against the Wattlebridge playbook. I have not seen the full SPA draft, so clause references are as the Seller cited them. The Seller's cross-references are inconsistent in places (for example, Bluefen is cited as both Clause 3 and 6.3), so the mark-up should confirm them.

## 1. Departures at a glance

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Push back |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority, none given) | Reject. Restore 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Restore AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Restore AUD 50,000 tipping basket. |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with written approval, none given) | Reject. Restore 24 months. |
| Time-limit "applies to all Claims" | Blanket override | No hidden general-regime override | Reject. Each category keeps its own regime. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same cap and time limits as general | 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Reject. Separate regime. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable | Reject. Add the carve-out. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket exclusion, including data-room and public-record matters | Delete; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry | Delete. |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence of conditions satisfied before Completion | Reject. |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release provided after Completion | Payout from Completion funds; effective releases; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Reject. |
| Funds flow / DD-005 bonuses | Not itemised; "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs | Reject. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure | Reject. |
| DD-006 export incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Investigate, preserve logs, require updates; assume no confirmed breach either way | Do not accept materiality conclusion. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic debt or price deduction | Assess; do not accept the characterisation. |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain open; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution | Reject. |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required | Reject as sole evidence. |

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

**Liability architecture (cap, thresholds, time limits).** The Seller's package is worse than our fallback on every quantitative term at once: a lower cap, a higher de minimis, a larger deductible basket and a shorter claims period. Our playbook fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months) are conditional and require Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft. None has been given, so the Seller's numbers should not be treated as movement. Converting the basket to an excess-only deductible also removes the first-dollar recovery we require. Together these changes would significantly reduce the recovery available on a general warranty claim.

**Collapsing the regimes.** The Seller's proposals to apply general caps and time limits to Title and capacity, and to apply the limitations and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims", merge categories the playbook requires to stay separate. Title is a fundamental protection and should not sit under the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. The fraud carve-out is missing entirely from the Seller's text, which is a significant gap. Non-reliance combined with an exclusive-remedy clause and no fraud carve-out would leave the Buyer without recourse for deliberate misconduct, which the playbook says no one may waive.

**Disclosure and knowledge.** The Seller's general disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2) would disclose everything in the data room and public registers. Combined with Clause 8.3, which bars claims for anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records, the Seller would effectively convert the entire diligence record into a defence. This should be rejected in full. Specific disclosure against specific warranties is the only acceptable model.

**Bluefen (~30% of FY26 revenue).** The Seller's own disclosure (DL 2) confirms no final written consent and no evidence that conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied. "Reasonable endeavours" and "treated as satisfied on delivery" are not acceptable for a material customer consent. This should be a condition precedent, with effective consent and condition-satisfaction evidence delivered before Completion.

**Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m).** The Seller proposes a release after Completion. DL 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid. Payout should come directly from Completion funds, with effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither is currently in place.

**Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000).** The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but they are absent from the draft funds flow. DL 5 also says the disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. The funds flow must either itemise the bonuses and triggered on-costs or make them seller-funded, so they are not silently excluded. Continued-employment conditions should also be clarified, since they affect whether the amounts are payable at all.

**Ironquay IP.** The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is described as "adequate". DL 4 confirms no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The AUD 180,000 open figure is not independently verified, and we should not treat it as either confirmed or disproved. The indemnity should be broadened, and the SOW3 cure mechanism preserved.

**DD-006 export/privacy incident.** The Seller's statement that the matter is "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the record does not support. DL 6 says whether unauthorised access occurred, the exact scope and whether notification is required are all unknown. Under the playbook we assume neither a confirmed breach nor a numeric demand, in either direction. Practically, we should require log preservation, a completed investigation with a defined timetable, regular written updates and a clear allocation of any resulting costs under a separate indemnity category. We should not accept the Seller's materiality view.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** DL 8 says the three renewals are "related" and that the disclosure does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. The Seller's ordinary-course characterisation is unsupported. We should assess them properly and not automatically treat them as debt or deduct them from price.

**Title.** The Seller relies on DD-012, a share register supplied by the Seller. The playbook treats this as an internal source, not independent proof. We should require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as company and search register extracts, PPSR searches and verification of the share transfer chain.

**Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime". They are not settled, and under the playbook they remain open. We should not accept any implied cap or time limit on tax or IP claims, and we should not assume either unlimited liability or a resolution.

**Other items to diligence (not covered by playbook positions).** The office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9) may contain notice or consent provisions. The disclosure does not establish that consent is required for the share sale. We should confirm the position independently before Completion rather than assume either way.

## 3. Recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller's update as a basis for negotiation.** Restore the playbook positions: 25%/AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24-month general period.
2. **Keep categories separate.** Title and capacity get a 100% cap, six-year minimum and sit outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Tax and IP remain open.
3. **Add a fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
4. **Limit disclosure** to specific fair disclosure. Reject data-room, public-register and Accounts deemed disclosure.
5. **Delete Clause 8.3.** Any knowledge qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
6. **Make Bluefen a condition precedent** requiring effective consent and evidence that conditions are met before Completion.
7. **Require Riverlark payout at Completion** from the funds flow, with effective security releases. Do not accept post-completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's written approval.
8. **Itemise the AUD 420,000 bonuses** and on-costs in the funds flow, or make them seller-funded.
9. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** beyond SOW3 and preserve the SOW3 cure. Do not treat AUD 180,000 as verified.
10. **For DD-006,** require log preservation, an investigation timetable and regular updates. Do not accept "not material".
11. **For Sandbar,** assess the three renewals. Do not classify them as debt or deduct from price automatically.
12. **For title,** require independent evidence beyond DD-012.
13. **Confirm lease and Mossvale** consent requirements independently.
14. **Escalation:** Any fallback to 20%/AUD 4.8m or 18 months requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given, so no such concession should be offered in this round.
=== END ADVICE ===
